newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end lower across the board.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end lower across the board.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed lower across the board on Monday, erasing earlier price gains, and volume was thin as market participants were sidelined ahead of a Japanese market holiday on Tuesday, traders said.
Prices were 50 to 90 yen lower, with the benchmark May 1998 contract down 60 yen at 15,650 yen per tonne. The daily volume was 36,684 lots.
All contracts opened higher, due to the Chicago market's price gains on Friday and the weaker yen against the dollar, traders said. But light technical selling capped the topside later, they said.
The Tokyo corn futures market will be closed on Tuesday for a national holiday. Trading will resume on Wednesday.

The spot May contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was trading at $2.92-1/2 per bushel at 0745 GMT, down from $2.94-1/2 at Friday's close. Spot May CBOT soybean futures were at $8.66-3/4 a bushel, down from $8.67-3/4 at Friday's close.
